text:
Alyssa: FYI just did a quick bring-up for polestar-small (open checkpoint + int8 ONNX) and seeing a weird recall@10 drop on short queries compared to baseline. clusters look OK overall but a chunk of anchors moved. anyone else seeing this? :eyes:
Ben: can you paste the numbers? short queries = how short?
Alyssa: baseline (fp16): R@1 0.42 R@5 0.66 R@10 0.73. polestar-int8: R@1 0.38 R@5 0.61 R@10 0.66. drop concentrated for queries length <= 6 tokens. full-query metrics mostly unchanged.
Maria: interesting. did you L2-normalize before and after quant? that often matters with cosine.
Alyssa: yes we normalized on index and queries pre-quant and post-quant. but i noticed the scale distributions shifted — some dims get clamped more.
Kai: could be per-channel scale mismatch after quantization. int8 asymmetric vs symmetric changes dot product geometry. did you try re-normalizing only after dequant?
Alyssa: re-normalizing after dequant didn't fully recover. tried per-vector renorm and per-dim shift; small improvement (~+0.02 R@10) but not to baseline.
Ben: can you share the eval command and a minimal snippet?
Alyssa: paste below (ran locally):
```bash
python eval_embeddings.py --model polestar-int8.onnx --index shards/qa_index --queries queries_short.json 
```
and the snippet we use to batch & quantize:
```py
# simplified
vec = model.embed(texts)
vec_q = quantizer.quantize(vec, dtype='int8', per_channel=True)
vec_deq = quantizer.dequantize(vec_q)
vec_norm = vec_deq / np.linalg.norm(vec_deq, axis=1, keepdims=True)
```
Maria: did you try disabling per_channel quant and use per_tensor? sometimes per_channel helps but if scales are noisy it can hurt short-query signal. also check bias folding in ONNX export.
Alyssa: per_tensor made it worse. per_channel seemed better but still bad. i also tried float16 export -> float16 matched baseline within noise.
Kai: float16 matching suggests quantization is the culprit. we should try calibration with a heldout set to compute quant scales using a representative sample (short queries heavy).
Ben: agree. also try a tiny additive bias correction: compute mean vector difference between fp16 and int8 deq on a calibration set and subtract that mean from int8 vectors (whitening/centering trick). that helped us once for cascade model.
Alyssa: i ran a quick calibration of 2k short queries and applied mean shift -> +0.03 R@10 (now 0.69) but R@1 still low. silhouette and cluster purity for a few topics show centroid drift for some anchors.
Maria: can you share t-sne or UMAP snapshot? might be an angular distortion, not uniform shift.
Alyssa: uploaded a quick UMAP to the channel (link) and attached small table with per-topic R@10 deltas.
Kai: another experiment: try L2 renorm + temperature scaling before similarity (cosine_temp = 0.7) or use dot with learned scale. sometimes scaling fixes ranking order.
Alyssa: trying temp=0.8 now. quick run: R@10 jumped to 0.71, R@1 to 0.40.
Ben: small wins. would also run knn with larger ef/search param to ensure this isn't a retrieval tuning artifact. increase ef to 200 and rerun.
Alyssa: ef=200 didn't change much. so it's model-side.
Maria: for production, i'd add a post-quant scatter correction: find per-dim rescale vector s.t. var(int8_deq * s) ~= var(fp16). can be fit on calibration set.
Kai: also try asymmetric quant with zero-point per-channel removed (force symmetric) — sometimes zero-points introduce offsets that affect cosine.
Alyssa: good list. next steps I'm going to run: 1) per-channel symmetric quant + calib, 2) mean-shift + per-dim rescale, 3) small retrain/adapt of final norm layer if we can (1-epoch on calibration pairs). will report results.
DevBot: Deploy job polestar-int8-calib-01 started by Alyssa (job id j-8821).
Ben: thanks. if retrain helps, we can bake that into our quant pipeline. also add a short-query heavy eval to the onboarding checklist. :thumbsup:
Maria: +1 on checklist. also log the calibration sample distribution so future runs replicate.
Alyssa: noted. I'll post a short summary w/ numbers when jobs finish. thanks team. :pray:
